caption:
OpenAI is retiring ChatGPT's Advanced and Standard voice modes on December 11.
GPT-Live, the voice model it launched in July, becomes the default for everyone, and users are switched over automatically.
Live video and screen sharing stay on the old Advanced voice for now.

Will you miss the old ChatGPT voice?

Follow @neurafeed.ai for daily AI news.

Source: Interesting Engineering · Photo: Getty Images
threads_text: OpenAI is switching off ChatGPT's Advanced and Standard voice on December 11 and moving everyone to GPT-Live, the model that can listen and talk at the same time. OpenAI says almost every voice user already moved. Do you actually talk to ChatGPT out loud?

paragraphs.text: OpenAI plans to retire the Advanced and Standard voice modes in ChatGPT on December 11, 2026, according to a company help notice reported by Superpower Daily and Interesting Engineering. After that date, both options will no longer appear in the Voice section of ChatGPT's settings, and GPT-Live will become the default voice experience for affected users. OpenAI began notifying users about the change on November 10.

Until the cutoff, people who still use either of the older modes can keep their current settings. Interesting Engineering reported that no manual migration is needed: ChatGPT moves affected users to GPT-Live on its own, and they do not have to start new chats or move existing conversations.

OpenAI introduced GPT-Live in July 2026. TechCrunch reported at the time that the launch included two models, GPT-Live-1 and GPT-Live-1 mini, built to sound more natural and to handle turn taking better. The mini model replaced Advanced Voice Mode as the default in ChatGPT, while paid subscribers could use the larger GPT-Live-1.

GPT-Live is a full duplex system, which means it can listen and speak at the same time. OpenAI says this lets users interrupt more naturally and lets the assistant give short acknowledgments, such as a brief "mhmm," while the user is still talking. It can also pass complex questions or tasks that require action to OpenAI's text models while the spoken conversation keeps going.

OpenAI has described the older systems as more limited. Advanced voice processed audio directly but waited for the user to finish before replying. Standard voice chained three separate steps, speech recognition, text generation and speech synthesis, which OpenAI said added delay and lost information along the way.
What stays the same for now

Past voice conversations remain in ChatGPT's history. Users can continue them by typing or through the Live voice experience, but any new spoken replies in those chats will come from GPT-Live rather than the original voice model.

There are two exceptions. Live video and screen sharing will keep running on Advanced voice, because GPT-Live does not support those features yet, according to OpenAI. The company has not given a date for moving them to the new model. Voice conversations with custom GPTs will also keep using Advanced voice until the December 11 deprecation.

OpenAI says voice usage in ChatGPT has nearly doubled since GPT-Live launched and that virtually all voice users have already moved to it. Superpower Daily noted that these adoption figures come from the company and have not been independently verified. OpenAI also listed response depth, continuity across conversations and personalization as areas it is still working on, without promising they will be ready by the cutoff.

The change looks like a cleanup more than a new launch. With most voice traffic already on GPT-Live, keeping two older systems in the settings menu mainly adds choices that few people use. The people most likely to notice are those who preferred the slower, turn based style of the older modes, and developers who built custom GPT voice flows on Advanced voice.
The next thing to watch is when OpenAI moves live video and screen sharing to GPT-Live, since that is the last part of ChatGPT Voice still tied to Advanced voice after December 11.
